narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 55% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it judged you slightly more likely than not to have repayment difficulties. The strongest factor was the requested loan term: 48 months is far longer than the average of about 19 months among approved applicants, and a longer repayment period increased the perceived risk. The second most influential factor was your checking account balance of 0–200 DM; only 18.4% of approved applicants had this status, compared with 59.2% with no checking account, so this modest balance suggested a limited financial cushion and pushed the decision toward denial. Your employment history of 4–7 years was the third most important factor and worked in your favor, showing stability, but it was not strong enough to offset the first two concerns. To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, building a stronger checking account balance, and providing clear proof of stable income and employment. You could also ask the bank whether a co-applicant or guarantor would help, and reapply once your financial profile is stronger.
